title: It is 11pm. What is actually in your kitchen?
dek: The meals nobody watches you make, and what your default dinner says about how you handle everything else.

questions.prompt: It's 11pm. The fridge has eggs, half a lemon and something in foil.
You're hosting six people and one of them doesn't eat what you've made. You find out at the door.

options.label: There's always something in the freezer
Rewrite the menu in your head
Ask them to help. It becomes a thing

questions.prompt: The kitchen gives you one power:
I buy ingredients for a person I'm not yet.
questions.high: The fridge is a vision board

questions.prompt: Someone puts ketchup on the thing you spent two hours making.
The best meal is the one someone else cooks.
Your perfect Sunday involves a kitchen that smells like:

options.label: Something in a slow pot since ten
Whatever was in the fridge, fried
Nothing. The app says twenty-five minutes

questions.prompt: Rank what actually rescues a 10pm Tuesday.
questions.helper: Top of the list is what you reach for first.

items.label: A fridge with something in it
A recipe you know by heart

questions.prompt: I follow the recipe exactly the first time.
A dinner party should end with everyone still at the table.
You've been asked to bring a dish. There are twenty people.

options.label: Something that looks impressive and took ten minutes
Two bags of ice and a packet of something
A proper plan, a cooler, labels

results.name: Toast, Again
results.blurb: You have a default meal and you are at peace with it. It's fast, it's comforting and it has never once surprised you, which is the entire point. People tease you about it right up until the evening they need something easy too.
strengths: Fast when everyone else is deciding
results.watchOut: Easy is a habit that can hide a bad week. Add one green thing on purpose.

results.name: The Fridge Archaeologist
results.blurb: You open the fridge and build a meal out of whatever's left. Half a lemon, three condiments, a bendy carrot — somehow it works. You are unbeatable at leftovers and slightly frightening about expiry dates.
strengths: Finds the meal nobody else saw
results.watchOut: Some things should be thrown out. The foil is not a mystery to solve.

results.name: The Takeaway Loyalist
results.tagline: One app, one order, no regrets
results.blurb: You know exactly what you want and you know who makes it. There is a place, there is an order, and there is a person who recognises your number. Efficiency, not laziness — although you've stopped explaining that to people.
strengths: Supports the same small business for years
results.watchOut: The app is not the only kitchen. Cook one thing from scratch this month.

results.name: The Recipe Follower
results.blurb: You follow the method because the method works. Measuring cups, timers, the whole thing — and the result is consistent every single time. Your baking is trusted at parties and your notes in the margin are better than the recipe.
results.watchOut: The recipe can't tell you what you like. Break it once and see.

results.name: The Improviser
results.blurb: The recipe is a mood, the measurements are a suggestion, and the pan is hotter than it should be. Sometimes it's extraordinary. Sometimes it's a lesson. Either way you'll do it differently next time and enjoy the argument.
strengths: Turns a mistake into a new dish
Never makes the same meal twice
results.watchOut: Write down the good one, or you'll spend a year trying to recreate it.

results.name: The Feeder
results.tagline: Cooks for eight, eats standing up
results.blurb: Your instinct when anyone is upset is to put food in front of them. You always make too much, you always say it's nothing, and you are always the last person to sit down. Nobody leaves your kitchen hungry, including people who said they weren't staying.
strengths: Turns a bad day into a table
results.watchOut: You're allowed to be fed too. Sit down before the food goes cold.

results.name: The Meal-Prepper
results.blurb: There are containers, there is a plan, and Thursday is already handled. You don't do this because you love cooking — you do it because future you deserves a break. The fridge looks like a small, delicious spreadsheet.
strengths: Saves money and time without fuss
results.watchOut: The plan can become the point. Leave one night unplanned on purpose.

results.name: The Standing Snacker
results.blurb: You eat over the sink, standing up, from a small bowl that becomes three small bowls. It's not a meal, it's a series of decisions. You are somehow never full and never actually hungry, and you own six types of crisp.
strengths: Never ruins their appetite for pudding
results.watchOut: A chair and a plate would fix half of this. Sit down for one meal.
